metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Morocco strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Hey Omar, have you thought about getting a bottle of champagne for Adam’s celebration? It might be a nice gift to commemorate his achievement. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: Uh, well... I don't really think that's appropriate. Champagne isn't a traditional gift in my culture. Maybe something more personal, like a nice pen or a book, would honor his achievement better. What do you think about that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I get that it might not be a traditional gift for you, but champagne could symbolize celebration, you know? It's about the moment. Plus, it doesn't have to be fancy, just something to toast with. Speaking of traditions, do you really think that making our parents proud should be one of our main goals in life? I mean, shouldn't it be about what we want?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I understand the symbolism, but... I just feel that making my parents proud is very important. In my culture, family is everything. Their support has shaped who I am. It's not just about what I want; it's about honoring them too. I think both aspects can coexist, don't you? But Adam's gift... I still prefer something meaningful.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I see your point about family being important, but I just can't agree that making parents proud should be a main goal. It feels like we should be focusing on our own paths instead. Anyway, about Adam's gift, how about we compromise? We could get the pen or book and maybe a smaller bottle of champagne for the toast? That way, we can celebrate and still have something personal. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: No, that's not how it works. In our way, making parents proud isn't just a nice idea; it's a *fundamental* part of life. To disregard that is, honestly, a bit naive. We don't just pursue our own paths without considering family. Actually, it's about respect and gratitude for their sacrifices. The gift should reflect those values, not just a trend. A pen or book *is* personal. We shouldn't dilute it with something that doesn't align with our values.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I understand you see it that way, but I really think it’s possible to honor ourselves and still appreciate our families. Life is about finding our own way, right? About Adam, I just think a mix of both could work. The pen or book is personal, but a little champagne could add to the celebration vibe. It’s not about it being a trend; it’s about having fun! Can we at least agree on that?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I get that you want to have fun, but I still believe that celebrations can be meaningful without compromising our values. Mixing gifts could send the wrong message, like we're prioritizing a party over respect. I just feel strongly about honoring our families in all we do. I appreciate your perspective, but I think we should stick to something that truly reflects Adam's achievement, without mixing in elements that don't resonate with my beliefs.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly

It’s important to have those moments of joy, too. I just don’t see how a little champagne takes away from the respect we have for Adam and his achievement. Why do you think it’s so hard to blend both ideas?

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I see your perspective, but for me, it's not just about blending ideas. It's about staying true to my values.
